pageCache.pageTitle: Hilltop First School - Parents in School
pageCache.text:
Parents in School
We value the links between parents and carers and school and have a number of occasions across each term were we welcome them into school.
Key Stage 1 Phonics / Grammar Fun - Fridays at 8:50
Parents and carers of pupils in Team Enchantment (Key Stage 1) are welcome to join in a weekly practical Phonics session each Monday morning after drop off. Elements of Spelling, Grammar and Punctuation are also practised during these sessions. They have proven to be very useful in helping parents to see first hand how they can help to support their children's learning in these areas whilst having fun.
Foundation Stage Song and Rhyme - Wednesdays at 8:50
All family members are welcome to join pupils in Team Woodland (Early Years Foundation Stage) immediately after drop off on a Wednesday morning for a session of songs and rhymes. Adults are encouraged to sing along with the children.
Grown Ups in Golden Time
Once each term, the parents and carers in each Key Stage are invited to join their children during Friday afternoon Golden Time. This is a chance for adults and children to interact and share the variety of games and activities in the classroom. Whilst playing in Golden Time, children are developing key social and language skills through playing with their peers. Games and activities are chosen to encourage creative problem solving, imagination, turn taking and cooperation.
Please check the school calendar for dates for each team.
We welcome parents and carers to join or team of adult volunteers who come into school regularly to support children's learning through a range of activities including listening to children read and playing games to practise turn taking, maths skills or phonics knowledge. All volunteers hold up to date DBS checks. Parents and carers who are interested in being involved in this way should contact the school office to obtain an application form.
For information about Hilltop Friends, please see the Hilltop Friends page on the website.
Information for Families
Parents in School

SEND Information
Hilltop is a mainstream school committed to providing the best learning experience possible for each of our pupils. We have been awarded the RBWM Inclusion Mark (November 2020).
"Quality First Teaching (QFT) is embedded in classrooms as can be seen by the teachers' planning and use of Reasonable Adjustments.... Communication within the school is excellent: The SENCo knows the pupils with SEND and families well, and makes herself available to
support staff if required. The joint planning between the teaching and support staff is particularly effective and this reflects the SENCos/ Headteacher's understanding of the importance of this."
"Pupils at Hilltop school love their school where they feel happy, safe and included."
RBWM Inclusion Mark Feedback November 2020
Our SEND Co-ordinator is Lynn Bima - Tel 01753 863502
Our Governor with responsibility for SEND is Darren James.

Our Rise and Shine club runs each morning from 7.30am until 8.40am (doors close at 8.20am). Rise and Shine is supervised by members of the Hilltop Support Staff. In keeping with current safety measures, pupils are grouped in Key Stage bubbles with pre-booking essential.

pageCache.text:
Dandelion Resource Base
Lead teacher: Mr Pohl
Support staff: Mrs Havercroft, Miss Moore, Miss Antonsen, Mrs Hunter, Miss Harpin
Our Dandelion Resource Unit which opened in September 2024, offers a maximum of ten places for children with an Education, Health and Care Plan where Speech, language and Communication is named as a primary need. This need may sit alongside a diagnosis of autism. The Dandelion lead teacher works closely with the SENCo to plan the curriculum, ensuring that the detail within children's EHCPs feeds into the daily provision.
The unit consists of two main learning rooms, a sensory room and a dedicated eating room. There is a small fenced-off outdoor area attached to the unit. The school day is built around consistent routines of short adult-led group and individual learning sessions and more child-led explore times. Termly topics provide a context for learning, but the essential curriculum is tailored around the development levels of the children and their individual 'next steps'.
A total communication approach is followed. Makaton and Widget symbols are used throughout the day and children are encouraged to communicate in a way that is right for them. Staff receive regular advice and continued professional development from a private Speech and Language therapist and the school's link Educational Psychologist. Staff follow therapy plans provided by CYPTS.
Places in Dandelion are allocated through the RBWM SEND team and children accessing this provision must already have an EHCP. Prospective parents are encouraged to discuss the possibility of a placement at Hilltop with their child's local authority EHCP coordinator before contacting the school.
Once a child has been offered a place in the Dandeion Unit, our staff team will work closely with parents to plan a positive transition package for the child. Usually, this includes a flexible soft start with a few short days before the child joins fulltime.

Admissions
As a maintained school, all admissions to Hilltop are processed and managed through the local authority, RBWM. For information related to all RBWM school admissions, please see the RBWM Website.
If you would like your child to attend our school, please see full details of our admission arrangements below.
If your child was born between 1st September 2021 and 31st August 2022 they will be due to start Reception in September 2026. Children born between 1st September 2022 and 31st August 2023 will start Reception in September 2027.
Parents are invited to visit the school for a tour and the opportunity to meet our Headteacher, Ms Lynn Bima. We are offer to a maximum of three sets of parents/carers at a time. We ask that children other than babes in arms are not brought along for school tours.
If you would like to visit Hilltop and meet our Headteacher please email the school office using office@hilltopfirst.co.uk. We strongly recommend that parents visit schools before making this very important decision. We are always delighted to show prospective parents around, and to answer any questions you may have. You may find our leaflet called Choosing a School helpful when looking at schools.
Applications for Reception places and above:
The Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead admissions team deals centrally with all applications from children of statutory school age for all the Borough’s schools:
The admissions window for children starting Reception in September 2025 has now closed. If you would like to make a late application please see the RBWM Admissions website. If you are not a resident of RBWM, please apply via your own local authority.
Please check the RBWM admissions website for dates and deadlines regarding 2026 admissions.
If your child was born before 1st September 2019, your application will be for a place in Year 1 or above. The Borough’s admission team also manages these applications, which are called In Year Applications. You will be notified by the admissions team if a place is available at Hilltop and then arrangements will be made for the child to visit us, for you to buy uniform and for a starting date to be agreed.

Home Learning
The purpose of Home Learning at Hilltop is to establish a routine of continued learning beyond school. This is particularly important as pupils move on to middle school after Year 4. We also believe it is a valuable way for parents and carers to remain aware of their children's progress in Core Subjects. Some key areas of learning are best consolidated through repeated practise. These form the focus of home learning.
Reading: all children are expected to read with an adult outside of school on at least 4 occasions each week. Children can earn bronze, silver and gold badges after meeting this target for 10 weeks.
Spellings: Each child from Year 1 has a personalised set of target words which they are learning to spell. Time is given in school to practise these spellings but we encourage parents/carers to support additional spelling practise at home.
Maths: A weekly Online MyMaths game/task is set for all children from Year 1. Pupils have a full week to complete this challenge. In addition all children from Year 1 have access to Numbots for practise of number bonds and TimesTable Rockstars for times table revision.
Written Prepare and Share English: A weekly written English task is set for all children from Year 1. Pupils are given a full week to complete this task. This piece of written learning is a key resource used in the Thursday English lesson and so will impact on participation if it is not completed and returned to school in time.
Parents / carers are encouraged to speak to class teachers if they are experiencing any challenges with regard to home learning.
The temporary provisions in the Coronavirus Act 2020 expired on 24 March 2022. As a result the Remote Education (England) Temporary Continuity (No.2) direction no longer has effect.
Attendance is mandatory for all pupils of compulsory school age. We will consider providing remote education to pupils in circumstances when in-person attendance is either not possible or contrary to government guidance.
occasions when the school leadership decides that it is not possible to open safely, or that opening would contradict guidance from local or central government
occasions when individual pupils, for a limited duration, are unable to physically attend their school but are able to continue learning, for example pupils with an infectious illness
In these circumstances, we will provide remote education as soon as reasonably practicable, though in proportion to the length of absence and disruption to the pupil's learning.
Parents of children in Nursery, please remember that Tapestry is a wonderful way for your child and their teachers to stay in touch. We would love to see your photos and stories about learning at home.
